arguments.value: 31-year-old pregnant woman at 24 weeks gestation presented with fever, vomiting, loose stools, progressive quadriparesis, and altered sensorium. She had severe hypokalaemia with respiratory and metabolic acidosis, requiring intubation, ventilatory support, and aggressive potassium replacement. Workup showed normal anion gap metabolic acidosis with hyperchloremia, positive urinary anion gap and alkaline urine suggesting distal renal tubular acidosis, and autoimmune markers SSA and RO-52 with history of dry mouth and dry eyes consistent with Sjögren’s syndrome. Fever evaluation was positive for IgM Leptospira. She improved with electrolyte correction, bicarbonate replacement, and treatment with ceftriaxone, and was later discharged and followed through delivery at 36 weeks.
